chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail al-Ju'fi and Abdul Karim ibn Amr and Abdul Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Noah (peace be upon him) carried in the ship the eight pairs about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Eight pairs, two of sheep, two of goats, two of camels, and two of cows.'

So, from the sheep, there were two pairs: one domestic pair that people rear, and the other pair were the wild sheep that are in the mountains, their hunting being lawful for them. And from the goats, there were two pairs: one domestic pair that people rear, and the other pair were the antelopes that are in the wilderness.

And from the camels, two pairs: the Bakhati and the Arab. And from the cows, two pairs: one domestic pair for people, and the other pair were the wild cows. And every kind of good bird, wild or domestic.
ai.seo_question: What specific animals did Noah carry in the Ark according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the composition of the 'eight pairs' in the Ark by categorizing them into domestic and wild counterparts across four quadruped families—sheep, goats, camels, goats, camels, and cattle—alongside birds. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the preservation of biological diversity and the distinction between tame and wild species as part of the divine plan for post-flood restoration. The narration serves to clarify Quranic ambiguity by linking specific animal types to their ecological roles, reinforcing the concept of intentional creation and preservation.

en.hubeali: H 14875 – Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Al-Ju’fy and Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, and Abdul Hameed Bin Abu Al-Daylam, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said:
‘Noahas carried eighty pairs in the ship about which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Said: “[6:143] Eight in pairs - two of sheep and two of goats [6:144] And two of camels and two of cows”.

So, from the pairs of the sheep were two sheep which were domestic ones which the people rear (keep), and another pair of sheep which were mountainous and wild sheep which are lawful to be hunted. And from the pair of goats, one was of the domesticated kind which the people rear, and another pair were the antelopes which are found in the wilderness.

And from the camels were two ‘’ Al-Bukhaty and the Arabic (camels). And from the cows, was a pair of the kind domesticated to the people and another pair of cows were the wild ones. And every kind of good birds, wild or domesticated.
en.sarwar: 428. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed, from the one whom he mentioned, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘
The water (of the storm of Noah (as)) rose above every mountain, and above every coast by fifteen cubits’.
